main_text.p: vertendo fuit genius singularis. propen[?]dit in hanc sententiam, tota ferè antiqui-tas. Clemens Alexandrinus Lucæ, Eu-sebius Clementi, interpretationis hasce tribuere partes. Hieronymus favet eidem Clementi, & de Paulo, eloquenter scrip-sisse in Hebraeo, ut eadem eloquentius ver-terentur in Græcum. Subscribit Theodo-retus, Argum. Epistolae, ἐρμηνείαν δὲ τῆς Ἑβραίων φωνῆς[?], ἣν φασὶ μεταχειρισάμενον τὸν Κλήμεν[?]ma. Accedunt, Chrysostomus, Oecumenius, Theophylactus, Ambrosius, Primasius, Haymo, & quotquot Veterum in Epistolas scripsêre, quorum longum foret reponere verba. Certatim huc confluunt neoterici scriptores. Baronius, solo hoc responso, egregiè se defunctum arbitra-tur, ad A.C.LX, Num.XLV. Nec improbat Bellarminus, citato loco de Verbo Dei L.1.C.XVII. prolixè Ribera proœm.in Epist. Et ne de plerisque pontificiorum dicam, suffragio solutionem suo muni-unt, Zanchius, Tract.de Script.S. Tomo VIII. Hyperius, prolegom.in Epist. Tossa-nus, similiter in proœmio, aliique bene multi,

page.notes: Top left page number read as 186; the first digit is bold and partly blurred, so verify. The running head is in italic and bold. The opening word "propen[?]dit" is blurred at the line end; the reading "propen" is inferred from "dit" on the next line. The Greek passage in the middle of the paragraph is hard to read; each word is a best reading and every uncertain letter is marked [?]. The Greek word split between "Κλήμεν" and "ma." may be "Κλήμεντα" or a different form, so check it. Italic is set for the names and for the phrase "eloquenter scripsisse in Hebraeo, ut eadem eloquentius verterentur in Græcum" and for "aliique bene multi"; these are visible in the scan but a few italic boundaries are approximate. The paragraph begins mid-sentence and continues onto the next page, so cont="true" is set. The last line, "multi,", is part of the running text and not a catchword.
